We are seeking an experienced and motivated Environmental Services Supervisor to join St John of God Bunbury Hospital on a permanent part-time basis, 60 hours per fortnight.

In this role, you will support the Coordinator Environmental Services to maintain a high standard of cleaning and waste management across all allocated areas by training, supervising and motivating the Environmental Services caregivers. You will ensure all tasks are completed in line with Standard Operating Procedures and cleaning schedules, contributing to a safe, hygienic and welcoming environment for patients, visitors and caregivers.

The Position

Ensure high quality cleaning and waste handling standards are met and consistently maintained in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures and cleaning schedules.

Ensure that all Environmental Service areas are adequately maintained.

Conduct cleaning and linen audits within scope of Standard Operating Procedures and provide timely feedback and support to caregivers.

Ensure that all departmental equipment is safe and in good working order and that any repairs or replacements are identified and remedied as a priority.

Ensure all Environmental caregivers observe personal hygiene and uniform standards.

Ensure all Environmental caregivers are aware of waste management policies and procedures and understand the correct management of all wastes and the need for clinical waste segregation.

Prepare and review rosters and leave requests in a timely manner.

As guided by the Manager, conduct performance management of Environmental Services caregivers.

Assess current processes and coordinate with the Manager any areas for improvement in order to enhance the quality of cleaning and waste handling services provided in the hospital.

Actively support and participate in accreditation.

The successful candidate will have previous experience supervising caregivers in a cleaning environment, with the ability to support and deliver effective training programs. They will demonstrate strong knowledge of cleaning chemicals, safe handling practices, and the correct operation of cleaning equipment, along with the capability to coordinate resources efficiently through roster planning and leave management. Well-developed verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills are essential, supported by proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

In addition, the candidate will show a strong commitment to improving productivity and service quality, with the initiative to identify opportunities for improvement within the department. They will demonstrate sound problem-solving skills and the ability to develop effective solutions, while fostering team development and maintaining staff trust and engagement. The role requires the ability to work under pressure, accommodate flexible hours and variable workdays, and apply occupational health and safety principles to ensure a safe working environment for themselves and others.

Above all, people will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

 Assisting qualified electricians with a variety of domestic electrical work. 
 Learning the fundamentals of electrical installations, maintenance and repairs.

 Punctual, reliable and motivated, with a strong work ethic and willingness to learn.

 Work alongside experienced electricians who will provide practical guidance and support.

Overview

Port Lincoln Hospital is a cornerstone of healthcare delivery across the Eyre Peninsula, and the people who keep it running behind the scenes are just as important as those at the bedside. If you take pride in a well-maintained environment and want your work to directly support patient care and staff safety, this role is for you.

What You'll Be Doing

Reporting into the facilities team at Port Lincoln Hospital within the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll maintain the physical environment that patients, visitors, and staff rely on every day. Your responsibilities will include:

Carrying out general internal and external facility maintenance, including minor carpentry, painting, and plumbing repairs

Performing mechanical maintenance and reporting or escalating issues as required

Managing grounds upkeep and rubbish collection to maintain a safe, presentable site

Logging and managing tasks using computerised maintenance systems and standard office tools

Demonstrated experience in building and grounds maintenance across a range of trades tasks

Ability to work with computer packages including Microsoft Word and Excel

Sound judgement and the ability to prioritise and act independently in day-to-day tasks

A practical, solutions-focused approach with a strong eye for safety and detail

SA Health offers more than a job - it offers genuine job security, access to salary packaging benefits that can meaningfully increase your take-home pay, and the satisfaction of contributing to a healthcare network that serves one of South Australia's most distinctive regional communities. Ready to Apply

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy. We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

  Senior Salesforce System Administrator  
 You know Salesforce is only as strong as the way it is looked after. 
 Clean access. Sensible configuration. Stable releases. Good support. Strong governance. A platform people can actually rely on. 
 That is what this role is about. 
 You'll be joining a Brisbane-based university using Salesforce across existing and new platforms, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. Some of the environment is established. Some of it is being improved and remediated. Your role will be to help look after the whole platform, not just one narrow part of it. 
 This will suit you if you are a hands-on Salesforce Administrator who likes ownership, cares about platform quality, and enjoys being close to the people who use the system. 
  The role  
 As the Senior Salesforce System Administrator, you'll help keep Salesforce stable, secure and useful across a large university environment. 
 You'll work across day-to-day administration, user support, configuration, platform improvement, release support and governance. 
 You'll be the person helping make sure Salesforce is well managed across CRM, marketing, engagement, alumni-style use cases and Education Cloud. 
 You'll work with the Salesforce Program Manager, architects, business analysts, DevOps specialists and business stakeholders. You won't be working in isolation, but you will be trusted to take real ownership of the admin layer of the platform. 
  What you'll be doing  
 You'll manage Salesforce users, roles, profiles, permission sets, licences and access controls. 
 You'll support Salesforce CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud usage across existing and new platform areas. 
 You'll provide practical support to users, helping resolve issues and improve how teams use Salesforce. 
 You'll configure Salesforce using declarative tools such as Flow, Approval Processes, Assignment Rules, Lightning pages, page layouts and permission structures. 
 You'll support sandbox management, release management and controlled deployment processes. 
 You'll help identify technical debt, platform risks, security issues and improvement opportunities. 
 You'll document changes, support adoption and create guidance that helps users get better value from Salesforce. 
 You'll help improve and remediate the platform while also keeping the current environment running properly. 
  What we're looking for  
 You'll bring strong hands-on Salesforce administration experience. 
 You might currently be a Salesforce Administrator, Senior Salesforce Administrator, Salesforce System Administrator, Salesforce Platform Administrator or Salesforce Consultant with strong admin capability. 
 Higher education experience would be useful, but it is not essential. 
 Experience in adjacent environments would be very relevant, particularly CRM, marketing, membership, alumni, engagement, customer service or stakeholder management platforms. 
 You'll be comfortable working in a complex Salesforce environment where different teams use the platform in different ways. 
 You'll understand Salesforce security, user access, profiles, permission sets, configuration, support and release processes. 
 Salesforce Administrator certification is preferred. If you are not certified yet but are actively working towards it, we are still happy to talk. 
  Why this role could be interesting  
 You'll have genuine ownership of a high-impact Salesforce platform. 
 You'll be involved in both improvement and remediation, not just routine ticket work. 
 You'll work across broad Salesforce use cases, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. 
 You'll be part of a major university environment where Salesforce supports real engagement with students, staff, partners and alumni. 
 You'll have the chance to help create a strong higher-ed Salesforce case study. 
  Location  
 The university is based in Brisbane. 
 Brisbane-based candidates are very welcome and would spend regular time in the office. 
 We can also consider candidates in Sydney, Melbourne or other eastern Australian cities, provided you are willing to travel to Brisbane occasionally. As a guide, there will be an expectation to attend the Brisbane office at least once per month.

An exciting opportunity exists to join the Nepean BPT Network as a Basic Physician Trainee.

The Nepean BPT Network may offer 1- or 2-year contracts (as required for completion of their length of training) to applicants who have completed their time in an accredited BPT role. Where you'll be working

The Nepean Basic Physician Training Network is a growing network that prides itself as a young, vibrant, enthusiastic and collegial unit with a total of 45 BPTs. Our program is designed to produce well rounded high quality Physicians that excel both from a professional and academic perspective. We find satisfaction in seeing our Trainees grow during their time with us and achieving personal and professional success. It is our privilege to have you join our team so that we can help you create your very own success story.

Nepean has full accreditation with the RACP as a Level 3 Hospital. Nepean offers a broad range of medical specialties including an ICU term.

BPTs may be required to undertake rotations to sites within the Network.
Ryde Hospital provides both inpatient and community services. It is a 180 bed acute care Hospital. Acute services include emergency, elective surgery, day surgery, maternity, orthopaedics, cardiac and intensive care. Non-acute inpatient services include aged care and rehabilitation, drug and alcohol and mental health.

Bathurst Base Hospital is a 100 bed hospital with 7 bed ICU-CCU, 25 medical beds. Full medical-surgical-paediatric-anaesthetic-ICU consultant rosters. Principal referral centres are Orange, Nepean and RPA.

Tweed Hospital is a regional referral, level 5 base hospital providing care to over 45,000 patients every year.

Lecture series with predominant focus on clinical topics.

Written exam preparation with MCQ sessions and trial exams.

Clinical exam preparation including:
Lectures focusing on clinical preparation

Boot camp

Public long cases

Weekly short cases

Regular neurology short cases

Scorpio sessions

Trial exam

Hospital wide teaching
Weekly Grand Rounds

ID-Endocrine-Neuro-Renal teaching

Division of Medicine meetings bi-monthly - Masterclass, M&M meeting

What you'll be doing

The primary purpose of the Basic Physician Trainee (BPT) is to provide effective medical services to patients under supervision, while developing expertise in medical practice in a complex clinical environment in inpatient and outpatient areas in the public health organisations within the Network.

Basic Physician Training roles consist of rotations through medical departments, working under an appropriate level of supervision by consultants. Rotations have different levels of responsibility and team structures. BPTs will gain increasing clinical autonomy and accountability as team leaders throughout the course of the up to three-year training program, building on their skills and attributes with the goal of entering an Advanced Training program.

BPTs undertaking the care of medical patients should ensure that they operate within their own level of expertise within a collaborative clinical care model and to seek consultation with the treating physician when appropriate, in the following activities:

Clinically assess patients, incorporating consultation-history taking, examination, and formulation of a differential diagnosis and management plans.

Discuss diagnoses and management plans with patients and their families or carers.

Document the progress of patients in multiple settings.

Prescribe medications tailored to patients needs and conditions.

Transfer care of patients.

Choose, organise and interpret investigations.

Assess and manage acutely unwell patients.

Plan, prepare for, perform, and provide after care for important procedures.

Job description:

 
We are seeking an experienced Specialist General Practitioner to deliver high-quality virtual and face-to-face care across Tasmania's Virtual Care Services and primary care settings.

 

 






 

The Team

Care@home is a state-wide interdisciplinary service that remotely supports patients, to better self-manage their illnesses and chronic conditions in their own home using virtual care technologies, improving patient health outcomes, and reducing potentially preventable hospital admissions.

This virtual care service has been established as a state-wide navigation hub, that provides a single point of access for home and community-based care; making it easier for both consumers and clinicians to identify what care pathways are available to support people in their preferred environment.

This interdisciplinary service employs General Practitioners who deliver virtual clinical consultations, support for GP Registrars and junior doctors and short- term primary care deployment to community settings where there are critical risks to the delivery of services.

The Role

The Specialist Medical Practitioner - General Practitioner is responsible for:

Providing specialised virtual care to patients enrolled in THS Virtual Care Services, managing non urgent acute and chronic conditions suitable for management in a home care environment.

Delivering a full range of virtual clinical services, such as triage, assessment, patient management plans, clinical governance, guidance, advice, support, and expert opinions.

Support private General Practice facing significant staffing challenges when no alternative solutions are available including the provision of face to face and virtual care consultations.

Provide interim supervision to GP Registrars, International Medical Graduates (IMGs), and Junior Doctors working in District Hospitals and temporary deployment to primary care in high-risk community settings.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in shaping best practice injury management and return to work outcomes across South Australia's regional public health system. As the Senior Return to Work Consultant, you will work collaboratively with injured workers, Senior Managers, Senior Claims Consultants and Human Resources to drive sustainable return to work outcomes, influence positive workplace culture and support worker wellbeing. You will provide expert advice on complex injury management matters while contributing to organisational performance, compliance and workforce capability. You will be part of a professional and supportive team, with the opportunity to build strong partnerships across regional Local Health Networks, government stakeholders, healthcare providers and external agencies, and making a meaningful difference to the health, safety and recovery of our workforce.

WHO ARE WE? 

The Rural Support Service (RSS) is a business unit in SA Health and provides services throughout regional South Australia to support the six regional local health networks (LHNs). It employs around 260 people who work in 37 regional, rural and remote SA locations, or in the RSS's three Adelaide offices. 

WHERE AND HOW YOU WILL WORK 

Many RSS staff enjoy working from home, from one of our Adelaide offices or any regional site, and benefit from the work-life balance this provides. They enjoy the freedom to further their career while remaining part of their local community and contributing to health care right across regional South Australia. 

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

Are you..

An experienced injury management and return to work professional with significant expertise in workers compensation, rehabilitation, return to work planning, and the management of complex physical and psychological injury cases.

A strategic and influential consultant who can provide expert advice to executives, managers, HR, WHS professionals and external stakeholders, driving best practice injury management outcomes across diverse and geographically dispersed workplaces.

An exceptional relationship builder with proven ability to develop productive partnerships with employees, managers, medical and allied health providers, unions, legal representatives and government stakeholders to achieve positive outcomes.

A proactive problem solver who can navigate sensitive and complex matters, identify barriers to recovery and return to work, and implement innovative solutions that support both employee wellbeing and organisational performance.

A resilient and adaptable leader with strong mentoring, project management and continuous improvement capabilities, who is committed to fostering capability, compliance and positive workplace culture across regional health services. 
If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will.... 

Deliver expert rehabilitation and return to work services, applying early intervention strategies and managing complex cases to maximise recovery, achieve sustainable return to work outcomes and minimise claim costs.

Deliver job-seeking services, where required, to place into new positions injured workers who cannot return to their pre-injury position due to their work-related injury.

Organise and host medical case conferences with injured workers, medical providers and (at times) unions and legal representatives, and achieve optimum outcomes.

Provide specialist advice and consultancy services to executives, managers, HR and WHS professionals on injury management, workforce wellbeing, dispute resolution and strategies to address complex workplace issues.

Develop and maintain strong stakeholder partnerships, working collaboratively with injured workers, managers, medical practitioners, allied health providers, unions, legal representatives and other parties to remove barriers and achieve positive outcomes for injured workers and the organisation.

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways: 

Opportunity to work from home or from an office, or both.

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information 

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities. 

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program. 

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families.

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following: 

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy. Further information is in the application for to help guide you. 

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. We continually look for ways to support and promote diversity and flexible ways of working so please let us know what interests you.

What You’ll Do 
 
This role is a full-time, permanent position based in Wollongong, NSW (postcode 2500), working within Sicona’s Pilot Plant facility. This role offers an annual salary package from $76,515 - $85,000 plus superannuation commensurate to the candidates experience and level of qualifications. As an entry level position, the candidate will be appropriately trained and supervised to operate within the Plant. You’ll contribute to Sicona’s long-term objective to deliver high performance battery materials at mass market scale, without costing the earth. 
- Support day-to-day operations and maintenance schedules as part of the engineering operations team.    
- Monitoring, adjusting and operating assets at operational sites to meet KPIs.   
- Support the design, procurement, installation, testing and commissioning of current and / or new facilities, as well as turnaround and inspection activities (T&I).   
- Identification of faults through the use of fault-finding techniques followed by troubleshooting and rectification of problems.

This includes managing relationships with various stakeholders and suppliers, evaluation of RFQs/RFPs, review of technical bids, and overseeing deliverables to align with project timelines and budgets 
- Support preventative and predictive maintenance programs, including maintenance planning and scheduling. 
- Contribute to project planning and execution by contractor coordination, proposal evaluation and deliverable monitoring. 
- Draft 2D and 3D models of equipment, spare parts and plot plans of facilities using the AutoCAD suite 
- Assist with raw material and final product inventory sample collections

What You will need to Succeed:  
Bachelor’s or higher degree qualification in Chemical, Process, Electrical, Mechanical or other related Engineering field. 
A “solution mindset” and able to manage varying tasks with often changing and competing priorities.  
Familiarity with PFDs, and P&IDs, HAZOP analysis, troubleshooting procedure. 
A team player attitude who can also take initiative independently. 
Adaptable mindset, and ability to adjust on the fly. Priorities change. You roll with it. 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills together with sound writing skills for reports and proposals.

Strong communication skills and comfort with digital tools like MS Office  
Experience in process operations, materials handling or supply chain in the same or similar setting
 
Even Better If You Have

Knowledge of gas cylinders, chemical handling, and analytical equipment.

Knowledge of Working in Hazardous Areas Classifications  
First Aid, Fire Safety training, Working at Heights, White Card, Forklift training  
 
Why join us?

Who We Are 
We develop next-generation silicon-carbon (Si/C) anode materials for lithium-ion batteries—designed to significantly increase energy density and improve fast-charging performance. That’s the kind of breakthrough that gets us out of bed. Check out our website to find out more about our awesome work: https://siconabattery.com.

This Is More Than Just a Job

Monash Health is a great place to work
Monash Health is Victoria’s largest and most comprehensive health service. For more than 170 years, Monash Health and its predecessors have provided safe, high-quality healthcare and service for people at every life stage. 
To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos: monashhealth.org/careers.
 
About Monash Doctors 
To help grow your career, there are more than 1,900 Junior and 1,700 Senior Doctors at Monash Health in over 200 medical specialties. We offer unparallel opportunities in Victoria's largest & most clinically diverse teaching health service. 
 
About Victorian Heart Hospital 
 
The Victorian Heart Hospital features a unique, holistic model of care with first ever cardiac services to provide tailored cardiovascular care for all Victorians, and specialised life-saving procedures for our community. As Australia’s only cardiac facility, housing world-ranking Monash University and the Victorian Heart Institute, the heart hospital represents a powerful model of collaboration, innovation and excellence and positioned to change the story of cardiovascular disease and accelerate its global reputation.  
 
Combining world-class clinical care, research, education and training, with inpatient and outpatient services, intensive care, cardiac emergency, surgical theatres, cardiac catheterisation labs, diagnostic imaging, cardiac clinics, rehabilitation, pathology and pharmacy, all in the same facility, to provide efficient and timely modern cardiac care. VHH is architecturally designed to enhance the patient experience in an open, warm setting with natural light and ready access to landscaped outdoor spaces to positively impact clinical outcomes. 
 
VHH is the largest cardiology service provider in Victoria with 270 staff across our four sites, providing over 80,000 episodes of cardiological care to the community annually. We provide cardiology healthcare services to patients of all ages, from in-utero and newborns right through to our senior citizens.  
Our mission is to improve community wellbeing through outstanding cardiology healthcare services and to provide exceptional quality education for our future healthcare professionals. 
 
About the role   
This position encompasses clinical, educational and research responsibilities. The incumbent will work as part of a multidisciplinary team in a busy teaching hospital environment (including Victorian Heart Hospital, Monash Clayton, Dandenong Hospital and Monash Casey (Berwick)), to provide safe and effective person centred care, provide teaching and supervision of resident medical staff and students and undertake training towards attaining Fellowship of the relevant college (if applicable).     
   
About You:   
To ensure your success in this role you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience and knowledge:  
  
•	Clinical skills and experience, ideally at the level of a medical registrar, 
•	Demonstrated ability to work efficiently, in a busy clinical environment, caring for unwell/unstable patients  
•	Strong communication skills, with a focus on clear, timely and respectful communication  
•	An ability to provide clinical leadership and coordinate patient care, whilst also supervising junior medical staff  
•	Demonstrate self-management; including an organised approach to work and education/training 
•	Demonstrate commitment towards key organisational initiatives, including VHH clinical trial research activities   
 
Mandatory requirements of the role:  
•	Primary medical degree (MBBS) or equivalent   
•	All candidates will require Australian working rights 
•	Registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)  
•	Employee Working with Children's Check? 
•	Current Drivers Licence 
 
Our Culture and Values 
At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 
 
Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 
 
You’ll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 
 
We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 
 
We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.  
 
How to Apply
Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system
Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.
